facts.f: A cricket team has 11 players on the field.
facts.e: The batting side has two batters at the crease at a time.

facts.f: A football team has 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.
facts.e: Only the goalkeeper may handle the ball, and only inside the penalty area.

facts.f: A field hockey team has 11 players on the field.
facts.e: Players may hit the ball only with the flat side of the stick.

facts.f: In kabaddi, each team has 7 players on the court.
facts.e: The raider must keep chanting 'kabaddi' while raiding.

facts.f: A basketball team has 5 players on the court.
facts.e: Basketball was invented by James Naismith in 1891.

facts.f: A volleyball team has 6 players on the court.
facts.e: Each team may touch the ball up to three times before sending it over.

facts.f: The Olympic symbol has five interlocking rings.
facts.e: They are blue, yellow, black, green and red on white, and stand for the five inhabited continents joined together.

facts.f: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
facts.e: They brought back the spirit of the ancient Greek games.

facts.f: The Summer Olympics are usually held every four years.
facts.e: The Winter Olympics are also held every four years, two years apart from the Summer Games.

facts.f: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal, in shooting, in 2008.
facts.e: He won the 10 m air rifle event at the Beijing Olympics.

facts.f: Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic gold in athletics, in the javelin throw.
facts.e: He won it at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, which were held in 2021.

facts.f: India has won eight Olympic gold medals in men's field hockey.
facts.e: The first came in 1928 and the eighth in 1980.

facts.f: Major Dhyan Chand is known as the 'Wizard' of hockey.
facts.e: India's National Sports Day, 29 August, is his birthday.

facts.f: India won its first Cricket World Cup in 1983, led by Kapil Dev.
facts.e: India won the 50-over World Cup again in 2011, led by M. S. Dhoni.

facts.f: Sachin Tendulkar was the first man to score a double century in a one-day international.
facts.e: He scored 200 not out against South Africa in 2010.

facts.f: Sachin Tendulkar scored 100 centuries in international cricket.
facts.e: He played international cricket for 24 years.

facts.f: Viswanathan Anand became India's first chess Grandmaster in 1988.
facts.e: He later became world chess champion five times.

facts.f: A chessboard has 64 squares.
facts.e: They are arranged in 8 rows and 8 columns of alternating light and dark squares.

facts.f: P. V. Sindhu won Olympic medals in badminton in 2016 and 2020.
facts.e: She became the first Indian woman to win two individual Olympic medals.

facts.f: The four tennis Grand Slams are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.
facts.e: Wimbledon is played on grass and the French Open on red clay.

facts.f: A marathon is 42.195 km long.
facts.e: This exact distance was fixed in 1921, based on the 1908 London Olympics course.

facts.f: The FIFA World Cup in football is held every four years.
facts.e: The first one was held in Uruguay in 1930.

facts.f: In 2009, Usain Bolt ran 100 metres in 9.58 seconds.
facts.e: It set a world record that stood for many years.

facts.f: M. C. Mary Kom won six world boxing championships and an Olympic bronze medal in 2012.
facts.e: She is from Manipur and is known as 'Magnificent Mary'.

facts.f: Milkha Singh, the great Indian sprinter, was called 'The Flying Sikh'.
facts.e: He won gold at the 1958 Commonwealth Games.

facts.f: P. T. Usha, the sprinter from Kerala, is called the 'Payyoli Express'.
facts.e: At the 1984 Olympics she missed a bronze medal by just one-hundredth of a second.

facts.f: In golf, the player who takes the fewest strokes wins.
facts.e: 'Par' is the usual number of strokes for a hole.

facts.f: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honour.
facts.e: The Arjuna Award honours outstanding athletes and the Dronacharya Award honours coaches.

facts.f: Manipur is known as a birthplace of modern polo.
facts.e: British officers learned the game there in the 1800s and spread it around the world.

facts.f: In kho-kho, each team has 12 players, and 9 take the field.
facts.e: Chasers sit in a line, facing alternate directions.

facts.f: A cricket pitch is 22 yards long.
facts.e: That is about 20.12 metres between the two sets of stumps.

facts.f: In tennis, a score of zero is called 'love'.
facts.e: The scores go love, 15, 30, 40 and game.

facts.f: The Paralympic Games are for athletes with disabilities.
facts.e: Javelin thrower Devendra Jhajharia won Paralympic gold medals in 2004 and 2016.

facts.f: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won a silver medal in weightlifting at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
facts.e: She lifted a total of 202 kg in the 49 kg category.

facts.f: The Olympic flame is lit at Olympia in Greece, using the Sun's rays and a curved mirror.
facts.e: It is then carried in a torch relay to the host city.

facts.f: Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal.
facts.e: She won bronze in weightlifting at the 2000 Sydney Olympics.

facts.f: In cricket, a hat-trick is when a bowler takes three wickets with three balls in a row.
facts.e: In football, a hat-trick is when one player scores three goals in a match.

facts.f: Kabaddi is a traditional Indian sport.
facts.e: It needs no equipment, just a court, two teams and lots of breath.

facts.f: Mallakhamb is a traditional Indian sport of gymnastics on a wooden pole or rope.
facts.e: Mallakhamb is the state sport of Madhya Pradesh.

facts.f: The four main swimming strokes are freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.
facts.e: Freestyle races are usually swum using the front crawl, the fastest stroke.

facts.f: Olympic gold medals are mostly silver.
facts.e: They must have at least 6 grams of gold plating on the surface.

facts.f: Golf balls have dimples to help them fly farther.
facts.e: The dimples change how air flows around the ball, reducing drag.
